# M3-7: Writer

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-7`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-7`
- Depends on: M3-0a, M3-1b
- Touches (exclusive while running): writer/, ynab/
- Plan refs: §1 `writer/`, §2 `write_log`, §3.2 step 4, §6 concurrency with human edits, R6b, R7, R7a, N9
- YNAB access: none (fakes only; live writes are M3-8)
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
`writer/` is the only path that categorizes in YNAB. Every write is logged before it's sent, locked fields are untouchable, and
a dry-run writer physically can't write.

## Scope
- `ynab/`: add a bulk transaction PATCH sending only the fields it changes (`category_id`, `approved`), marked as a write for the governor.
  Errors redacted, op strings fixed, ids never included.
- `writer.Apply(ctx, batch, actor, via)`:
  1. take a mutex (the scheduler and Slack goroutines both call it);
  2. re-sync through an injected function (§6);
  3. re-read each row and drop any that is locked, deleted, split, or whose category changed since the decision;
  4. insert `intent` rows holding before_json and after_json;
  5. PATCH; mark each row `done` or `failed` from the per-transaction response.
- Hard gates, all checked inside `Apply` under the mutex, for every caller including Slack answers:
  - `writer.Gate`, an atomic effective mode that starts at `dry_run`. It's updated per run through a setter (M3-14b), never fixed at startup. Anything but `auto` returns `ErrDryRun`.
  - A call for any plan other than the configured one is refused.
  - A transaction dated before `AutoSince` is refused (`ErrBeforeAutoSince`), judged from the re-read row.
- Slack answers: `actor` is the speaker, and the writer records a `slack` lock on the category field after `done`.
- Crash recovery: `Reconcile(ctx, syncStartedAt)` runs after a successful sync, never at process start, because the mirror doesn't show a PATCH until the sync brings the echo back. It takes the mutex and only judges unfinished `intent` rows created before `syncStartedAt`: `done` if the row matches after_json, else `failed`. Never re-send. `Apply` calls it after its own re-sync (step 2); M3-14b calls it after each scheduled sync.
- Governor budget exhausted or 429: the batch fails cleanly and is retried on a later tick.

## Out of scope
- Memo, flag, split or delete writes; assignment (M4); `revert_write` (M5). Live YNAB calls.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Test: a new Gate is `dry_run`; `ErrDryRun` with no HTTP call; flipping the Gate from `auto` to `dry_run` blocks the next `Apply`; another plan id is refused.
- [ ] Test: a row dated before `AutoSince` is refused with no HTTP call.
- [ ] Test: the request body has only the changed fields.
- [ ] Test: a row locked or edited during the re-sync isn't sent.
- [ ] Test: an intent row exists before the PATCH (fake asserts during the call); partial failure marks each row correctly.
- [ ] Test: crash after a successful PATCH: before the sync the intent stays unfinished; after the sync brings the echo it becomes `done`, and nothing is re-sent. Mirror mismatch after a sync gives `failed`.
- [ ] Test: an intent created after `syncStartedAt` isn't judged.
- [ ] Test: errors contain no id; concurrent `Apply` calls serialize (`-race`).
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `ynab/client.go`: `PatchTransactions` — one bulk PATCH (`/plans/{plan}/transactions`) sending only each change's set fields (`category_id`, `approved`) plus `id`; preflight and request marked as writes (`asWrite`); errors redacted, op text fixed.
  - `ynab/errors.go`: `NotApplied(err)` — true when a write provably changed nothing (budget exhausted, 429, 400/401/403/404/409); everything else (transport, timeout, 5xx, bad body) is "unknown".
  - `writer/gate.go`: `Gate` (atomic; new and zero value are `dry_run`), `Set`/`Mode`, modes `off`/`dry_run`/`auto`.
  - `writer/writer.go`: `Writer.Apply(ctx, Batch, actor, via)` and `Writer.Reconcile(ctx, syncStartedAt)` per the brief: mutex → gates → injected `Resync` → reconcile (intents older than the re-sync start) → gates again (a flip during the re-sync blocks) → re-read rows (missing, deleted, before AutoSince, any lock, split, category changed since `DecidedCategoryID`, no change, duplicate → skipped, not logged) → `intent` rows with before/after JSON and a shared `request_id` → PATCH → per-row `done`/`failed` from YNAB's answer → `slack` category lock after `done` when via is slack.
  - `writer/writer_test.go`, `ynab/client_test.go`: tests below.
- Acceptance:
  - Gate dry_run by default, `ErrDryRun` with no HTTP, auto→dry_run blocks next Apply, other plan refused → pass (`TestGate_NewIsDryRun`, `TestApply_GatesRefuseWithoutHTTP`)
  - Before `AutoSince` refused with no HTTP (also judged from the re-read row; empty AutoSince refuses all) → pass (`TestApply_BeforeAutoSinceRefused`)
  - Body has only changed fields → pass (`TestClient_PatchTransactionsSendsOnlyChangedFields` checks the wire JSON keys; `TestApply_SendsOnlyChangedFields` checks the writer's diff)
  - Locked/edited during re-sync not sent → pass (`TestApply_DropsRowsChangedDuringResync`)
  - Intent exists during PATCH; partial failure per row → pass (`TestApply_IntentBeforePatchAndPartialFailure`)
  - Crash after PATCH (simulated with `runtime.Goexit` inside the fake PATCH): stays intent until a sync; echo → done, mismatch → failed, nothing re-sent → pass (`TestApply_CrashAfterPatchThenReconcile`)
  - Intent created after `syncStartedAt` not judged → pass (`TestReconcile_SkipsIntentsAfterSyncStart`)
  - Errors carry no id (gate, AutoSince, PATCH errors and write_log.error text; plus `PatchTransactions` added to `TestClient_NoErrorPathLeaksIDs`); concurrent Apply/Reconcile serialize → pass (`go test -race ./writer ./ynab`, `TestApply_PatchFailures`, `TestApply_Serializes`)
  - Mutation-checked: removing the post-resync gate, the lock check, the created_at filter or the NotApplied branch each fails a test.
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` → pass
- Deviations from brief:
  - AutoSince is per row: rows before it are skipped and the rest of the batch still goes; `Apply` then returns an error matching `ErrBeforeAutoSince` (a one-row Slack batch gets exactly that). Empty `AutoSince` refuses every write (fail closed).
  - Only budget-exhausted, 429 and 4xx PATCH errors mark rows `failed`. A transport error/timeout/5xx may have landed, so its rows stay `intent` (error matches `ErrUnknownOutcome`) and the next Reconcile judges them against the mirror — never re-sent. Marking those `failed` would let M3-9 rule (b) read our own echo as a human first touch.
  - Any lock on the transaction (not only `category`) drops the row, since `approved` is the only other field written.
  - Reconcile also records the `slack` lock when it judges a Slack-originated intent `done`.
  - Reconcile only judges this writer's rows (configured plan, `Endpoint = "PATCH /plans/{plan}/transactions"`).
- Follow-ups for backlog: none
